_readme: THE VS CODE MCP CONFIG. VS Code agent mode reads .vscode/mcp.json and
ignores every other host's file, so the se lane needs its own copy.
The extension places it at workspace/.vscode/mcp.json on every
activation, the same declarative way RUNME places the other cages.
IT ATTACHES, IT DOES NOT SPAWN. The extension owns the ONE se server
(HTTP on localhost:7333); agent mode connects to /mcp there. A spawn
here would raise a second engine with a second walk beside the real
one - the exact split the shared server exists to prevent.
THE CAGE DEPENDS ON HOW THE SESSION WAS OPENED, and this file used to
say flatly that there was none. Both halves matter:
STARTED BY THE PLAY BUTTON - CAGED. The extension calls
workbench.action.chat.open with toolsExclude, built from
copilot-cage.json's exclude_args (vscode/extension.js,
openCopilotInChat). Tools are excluded BY NAME, as on the CLI.
OPENED BY HAND FROM THE CHAT PANEL - NOT CAGED. Nothing passes
toolsExclude, so native file and terminal tools stay visible. Native
web search is allowed in either launch mode; project search is not.
A reader cannot tell from inside which session they are in, so behave as
if uncaged either way: use the se lane, every time.
VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING IT, the same empirical way copilot-cage.json was
verified: open a session EACH WAY and ask it to list the exact names of
every tool it can see. Anything except se_ tools and native web search
is a hole.
